The correct local date governs what corroborating records (badge access, calendars, travel, physical presence) we ask for, and it bears on ¶ 48's “approximately one week before his last day” framing.

T-20  What Meridian systems hold engineering data from 2018 to the present, what retention or auto-deletion applies to each, and has anything been suspended?

Source: White paper § 7.2 (development from April 2018) defines the period that must be preserved; Exhibit F Row # 40 shows SkyVault instructing its own IT to “preserve all logs and endpoint data per litigation hold” on 02/12/2018, an asymmetry worth noting.

Evidentiary purpose: Preservation scope is the most time-sensitive item in the entire investigation. Any auto-deletion still running on a relevant system is an emergency, not an interview topic.

T-21  Could this team reconstruct, from surviving records alone, a module-by-module provenance narrative — and where are the gaps?

Source: White paper § 7.2 sets out the provenance narrative Meridian has already published; Complaint ¶¶ 54, 119 and 120 contest it.

Evidentiary purpose: Identifies, before any external deadline, which parts of the published account are documented and which rest only on recollection. The gaps determine where expert work and further collection are needed.

VI.  Witness Category 3 — Meridian's Legal Lead

Meridian's legal lead — identified in our materials as Jordan Kessler, VP of Legal, who was copied on outside counsel's April 5, 2024 response — is interviewed for a different purpose than the other two categories. This witness is the custodian of the company's factual record about how the dispute was received, routed, preserved and responded to, and the person best positioned to map Meridian's policies, agreements and systems. That value comes with the sharpest privilege constraints in this round: the same conversation that yields discoverable facts about dates, custodians, policies and systems will run continuously along the boundary of attorney–client communications and work product, and the interviewer must police that boundary in real time rather than sort it out later.

A.  Discoverable Factual Events, Records and Systems

L-1  Describe the intake of SkyVault's March 12, 2024 letter — when it arrived, in what form, who received it, how it was routed internally, and what was calendared as a result.

Source: Complaint ¶ 61 (letter dated March 12, 2024, sent by Callister, Voss & Greenbaum LLP to CEO Priya Chandrasekaran at Meridian's Austin headquarters, identifying the three patents-in-suit and making three demands) and the April 5, 2024 letter (acknowledging receipt and responding within 24 days). The March 12, 2024 letter is not in our file.

Evidentiary purpose: Receipt and routing are objective events, not privileged communications, and they fix the notice date underpinning the willfulness allegations in ¶¶ 63, 70, 78 and 86.

L-2  Identify the date any litigation hold issued, the custodians it reached, the systems and date ranges it covered, whether it has been refreshed, and whether automatic deletion was suspended on each system.

Source: Exhibit F Row # 40 shows SkyVault's counterpart step — “IT to preserve all logs and endpoint data per litigation hold”, dated 02/12/2018 — and Row # 50 records the matter's referral to SkyVault's litigation counsel on 02/16/2018; Complaint ¶¶ 61–63 establish that Meridian was on notice no later than March 2024.

Evidentiary purpose: The existence, date, distribution and scope of a hold are ordinarily discoverable even where the notice's text is withheld, and they are the first thing an opponent probes on a spoliation theory. Ask for the operative facts; do not ask the witness to recite counsel's drafting deliberations.

L-3  What preservation or collection steps, if any, were taken in 2018 at Meridian's formation, and was there any communication with SkyVault at that time?

Source: Complaint ¶ 53 (Meridian co-founded on or about April 11, 2018, roughly two months after Holt's February 16, 2018 departure); Exhibit F Row # s 45 and 50 show SkyVault engaging forensic examiners and litigation counsel in February 2018.

Evidentiary purpose: Establishes whether Meridian's duty to preserve was ever triggered in 2018 and what, if anything, from that period survives — the earliest and most probative window for the independent-development account.

L-4  What records-retention schedule applied between 2018 and 2024 to source control, email, chat, ticketing and build logs?

Source: White paper § 7.2 (development from April 2018 through the 2021–2022 enhancements) defines the period at issue; Complaint ¶ 54 makes the 2018–2020 development chronology central.

Evidentiary purpose: Retention periods determine what can still be recovered. A three-year chat retention policy, for example, would silently have destroyed the most contemporaneous record of the 2018–2019 design work.

L-5  Identify and produce the internal compliance processes referenced in the April 5, 2024 letter — what written policies exist, when each was adopted, who owns it, and how compliance is audited.

Source: The April 5, 2024 letter, third substantive paragraph: “Meridian maintains robust internal compliance processes designed to safeguard against the unauthorized use of third-party intellectual property.”

Evidentiary purpose: A representation has already been made in writing to opposing counsel. The underlying policies are ordinary business records, not privileged, and either substantiate the statement or reveal an exposure the partner must know about immediately.

L-6  What does Meridian require of employees on intellectual property — assignment agreements, prior-invention disclosures, confidentiality undertakings — and does a complete set exist for Dr. Holt and for the early engineering hires?

Source: ECIAA §§ 5.1–5.4 illustrate the structure SkyVault used, including the Exhibit A prior-inventions mechanism; ECIAA § 7.1 (twelve-month non-solicitation running through February 16, 2019); Complaint ¶ 130 alleges Meridian knew of Holt's ECIAA obligations and induced and benefited from the breach.

Evidentiary purpose: Meridian's own onboarding paperwork is the most direct evidence of the company's practice and of whether it inquired into Holt's prior obligations. It also identifies any hire that could implicate the unpleaded non-solicitation provision.

L-7  Who approves the introduction of open-source or third-party components, is approval logged, and do the approval records go back to 2018?

Source: White paper § 4.2 and § 7.2 (reliance on publicly available implementations including DroneNav) and Reference 2; the April 5, 2024 letter's compliance representation.

Evidentiary purpose: Bridges the technical and legal records: an approval log converts the white paper's narrative attribution into a documented, auditable decision trail.

L-8  Identify the fact and timing of any intellectual-property diligence conducted for the March 2023 Series B round, who conducted it, what categories of materials were furnished, and what confidentiality or common-interest agreements govern those materials.

Source: Complaint ¶ 12 (a $35 million Series B round led by Ridgepoint Ventures in March 2023, and 2023 revenue of approximately $19.4 million, both pleaded on information and belief in part).

Evidentiary purpose: Diligence files often contain the earliest contemporaneous written statements about technology provenance, made long before any dispute. Disclosure to investors also raises waiver questions that must be scoped before anything is produced or relied upon.

L-9  Identify every person with factual involvement in responding to the SkyVault allegations, separating those who acted at counsel's direction from those who did not.

Source: The April 5, 2024 letter (signed by Laura Brackwell of Brackwell & Haines LLP, copied to Jordan Kessler, VP of Legal) and Complaint ¶ 62 (describing the response as coming from Meridian's outside counsel).

Evidentiary purpose: Sets the custodian list and draws the privilege perimeter before substantive questioning begins. People acting at counsel's direction are in a different position from those who merely collected records.

L-10  What communications has Meridian had with Dr. Holt regarding his SkyVault obligations — at hiring, at any point thereafter, and since March 2024?

Source: Complaint ¶ 130 alleges that “Meridian was aware of Holt's obligations under the ECIAA and induced, participated in, and benefited from Holt's breach”; ECIAA §§ 3.1, 3.5 and 5.2 define the obligations in question; Complaint ¶ 53 places Holt's arrival at Meridian in April 2018.

Evidentiary purpose: Company knowledge of the ECIAA is the hinge of the inducement theory. Pre-litigation communications on the subject are largely non-privileged and may be the best evidence either way; post-March-2024 communications will mostly be privileged and should be logged rather than explored.

L-11  Was Meridian ever given a copy of the ECIAA, and if so, when, by whom, and what was done with it?

Source: The ECIAA is pleaded as Exhibit E to the Complaint; Complaint ¶ 130 alleges Meridian's awareness of its terms.

Evidentiary purpose: A discrete, verifiable fact that either supports or defeats the knowledge element of ¶ 130, and that can be confirmed against onboarding files and email archives.

L-12  Has any insurance policy been noticed, and does Meridian owe indemnities to PathForge customers that these allegations could trigger?

Source: Complaint ¶¶ 59 and 146 (in excess of $50 million in cumulative PathForge revenue) and the Prayer for Relief (injunctive relief against further making, using and selling, plus damages of no less than $25 million); white paper § 1 (over 60 commercial customers).

Evidentiary purpose: Not liability evidence, but it drives notice deadlines and customer-communication obligations that have their own timing consequences.

B.  Matters Presumptively Protected — Handling Protocol

The following topics should be raised only to establish the threshold facts identified, and then stopped. Where the witness begins to disclose the substance of legal advice, counsel's requests, or counsel's mental impressions, the interviewer should note the topic for the privilege log and move on. The distinction to hold in mind is between the occurrence of an event (generally discoverable) and the content of a privileged communication about it (generally not).

L-13  Has Meridian obtained any written opinion of counsel concerning the '561, '227 or '889 Patents, and if so, on what dates? Please do not describe its content.

Source: Complaint ¶¶ 69–70, 78 and 86 allege willful infringement based on Holt's asserted knowledge and on notice from the March 12, 2024 letter, and ¶ 70 adds that Meridian continued “without any apparent attempt to design around … or obtain a license”; the April 5, 2024 letter denies infringement and reserves invalidity and unenforceability defenses.

Evidentiary purpose: The existence and date of an opinion are threshold facts the partner needs in order to evaluate a possible advice-of-counsel defense. Electing that defense would waive privilege over the subject matter, so the content must not be explored in this interview and the election is the partner's decision, not the witness's.

L-14  Has Meridian conducted or commissioned any technical comparison of PathForge against AeroCore, the patents-in-suit, or the deposited copyright material — and if so, when, by whom, and at whose direction?

Source: Complaint ¶¶ 116–119 (the copyright registration TX 9-142-338 covering AeroCore Firmware Suite v2.0, issued April 3, 2023, and the substantial-similarity allegation) and the claim chart following ¶ 67; the April 5, 2024 letter states that SkyVault's letter supplied no claim-by-claim analysis and that Meridian is “aware of none.”

Evidentiary purpose: Distinguishes protected litigation analysis from any ordinary-course engineering comparison, which may not be protected at all. Establish which category any such work falls into before it is described.

L-15  Who supplied the factual predicates for the independent-development statement in the April 5, 2024 letter, and what documents were reviewed — identifying people and documents only, not counsel's analysis of them?

Source: The April 5, 2024 letter: “Meridian independently developed its PathForge platform through the efforts of its engineering teams”, together with its reservation of an independent-development defense.

Evidentiary purpose: Meridian has asserted independent development in writing. The identity of the people and documents behind that assertion is the roadmap for corroborating it; the reasoning behind it is protected. The phrasing of the question is what keeps the two apart.

L-16  Has the question of separate counsel for Dr. Holt been evaluated, and does leadership understand that he faces potential individual exposure?

Source: Complaint Count VII (¶¶ 126–132) pleads breach of the ECIAA by Holt while seeking to hold Meridian liable for it, and Counts IV and V (¶¶ 94, 107) allege that Holt personally misappropriated the trade secrets; ECIAA §§ 8.1–8.3 provide for injunctive relief and fee-shifting against the employee; the April 5, 2024 letter responds on behalf of “Meridian and its officers and directors.”

Evidentiary purpose: This must be resolved before the Holt interview. Holt is both Meridian's CTO and the individual whose conduct is the subject of the claims; a conflict surfacing after his interview could compromise the privilege over it and the usability of everything he says. Upjohn warnings are necessary but may not be sufficient.

L-17  Has the request that SkyVault not contact Meridian's officers and employees been communicated internally, and what protocol applies to former employees, who are outside that request?

Source: The April 5, 2024 letter (requesting that SkyVault and its counsel refrain from contacting Meridian's officers and employees directly and directing all correspondence to Brackwell & Haines LLP).

Evidentiary purpose: Former employees are ordinarily reachable by opposing counsel. Knowing who they are, and whether any has already been approached, is both a witness-protection and an information-security question.

L-18  Did any without-prejudice discussions in fact occur following the April 2024 exchange, and if so, when, with whom, and under what confidentiality terms?

Source: The April 5, 2024 letter (offering to “arrange a call or meeting at a mutually convenient time”, made “without prejudice” and “subject to applicable rules governing settlement communications”); Complaint ¶ 62 characterizes the response as a categorical refusal to comply with any demand.

Evidentiary purpose: Whether a settlement track ever opened is a fact the partner needs for posture and for scheduling. The content of any such discussion is separately protected and should not be explored here.

VII.  Recommended Sequencing

We recommend interviewing Meridian's legal lead first, the technical team second, and Dr. Holt last, for reasons that are practical rather than formal. The legal lead should go first because that interview is the only one that can set the privilege perimeter before anyone generates a witness statement: it confirms that a litigation hold is in place and that auto-deletion has been suspended (L-2, L-4, T-20), produces the custodian and systems map the other two interviews depend on (L-9), and — most importantly — forces resolution of the separate-counsel question for Dr. Holt (L-16) before he sits, since a conflict surfacing afterward could compromise the privilege over his interview and the usability of everything he says. The technical team should go second because it is the records-bearing group: its answers convert assertions into artifacts — repository history and earliest commits (T-4, T-5), dependency manifests and the DroneNav question (T-6), a defensible search for the three named AeroCore file names and for SkyVault-origin strings (T-7, T-15), the search for the four claim-chart component names absent from the white paper we hold (T-12), and a practitioner's reading of the 4,700-file record and its time-zone and overlap problems (T-16, T-17, T-19). Those results are precisely the material against which Dr. Holt's recollection can be tested. He goes last because he is the only witness whose knowledge spans all six lead families and the only one who is personally the subject of the central allegations; his account should be taken against a documentary record already assembled rather than be allowed to define what we then go looking for, and the questions that matter most — the evening of February 8–9, 2018 (H-5), the eight-week pre-incorporation window (H-18), the eight distinct states of DroneNav use and non-use (H-37), and whether any SkyVault material ever reached Meridian (H-28) — can only be asked open-endedly once, and are worth far more when we can immediately test the answers. This order is not the only defensible one, and two contingencies would displace it: if the legal lead's interview reveals that no hold issued or that a relevant system is still deleting data, preservation triage takes priority over every scheduled interview; and if Dr. Holt retains separate counsel, we should take a limited, conflict-cleared preliminary session with him covering only device custody and preservation (H-6, H-11), and defer the substantive families until his counsel is in place.
